# Bank Transfer Process Plan

Reusable planning logic for clauses operating within a Bank Transfer Contract. It validates transfer policy and produces connections, state declarations and handlers for installation. A generated transfer request still requires a separate, authorized bank outcome. All paths refer to the instruction document where the plan executes.

## Configuration and conditional requests

- `parameters.method` accepts `bank-transfer` or `conditional-bank`, defaulting to `bank-transfer` when omitted. The containing document must match Bank Transfer Contract.
- `parameters.transfer` defaults to an empty object. Its `mode` accepts `workflow` or `when`, defaulting to `workflow`. Both retain inherited connection planning; `workflow` adds no conditional transfer machinery.
- With `mode: when`, `transfer.when` must exist and `transfer.requestId` must be nonempty text. Request execution additionally limits that identifier to 128 characters.
- `parameters.sources` defaults to an empty dictionary. Every alias read through `/sources/<alias>/...` in `transfer.when` must be declared there. The predicate permits static, non-root document paths and a restricted set of pure comparisons, Boolean operations, collection checks, identity reads and addition/subtraction. `$nodeBlueId` must directly wrap a `$document` read. Dynamic paths, unsupported operators and excessive nesting are rejected; `$literal` contents remain literal data.

In `when` mode, the plan declares `/paymentProcess_{clauseKey}/transferAllowed` with initial value `false` and sets `/paymentTerms/transferGate` to that path. An existing different gate causes `PAYMENT_POLICY_GATE_CONFLICT`. The initial value applies when the planned state is installed; absence is not an implicit `false`.

Generated handlers reevaluate eligibility on changes to `/payment`, `/bankTransfer`, `/activation`, `/sourceLinks` and the predicate's document paths. A nonempty `parameters.sources` also adds an Embedded Node Channel handler. Eligibility requires `/activation/active` to equal `true`, `transfer.when` to evaluate exactly to `true`, and—when `/clauses/documentSources` exists—`/sourceLinks/ready` to equal `true`.

The automatic request step proceeds only when the gate is `true`, `/payment/accepted` is `true`, `/payment/closed` is `false`, and `/bankTransfer/status` is `idle`. Otherwise it returns without requesting a transfer. It calls Bank Transfer Functions with the configured `requestId` and `sourceMode: event`, which allows this configured rule to request without a payer workflow call. The gate expresses policy eligibility, not completion or a person's permission. The supplied definitions establish `idle` as a prerequisite but do not show bank-transfer state initialization.

## Request and outcome meaning

The public `requestTransfer` operation is assigned to the payer channel and checks it against `/paymentTerms/payerChannel`. A new request requires instruction acceptance, source readiness when applicable, an open payment and any configured transfer gate. Its input contains only `requestId`; amount and currency come from `/paymentTerms/amountMinor` and `/paymentTerms/currency`.

A successful new request records `/bankTransfer/requestId`, changes `/bankTransfer/status` to `requested`, and emits a Bank Transfer Event with `kind: Transfer Requested`. This records an intention, not transferred money. After the source, actor, acceptance and identifier checks, the same recorded identifier returns `duplicate` without another request; a different identifier is rejected. The automatic handler does not request again after status leaves `idle`.

`confirmTransfer`, `declineTransfer` and `reportTransferUnknown` are guarantor operations checked against `/paymentTerms/guarantorChannel`. Each requires the recorded `requestId` and a nonempty `reference` of at most 256 characters. Confirmation also requires `amountMinor` and `currency` to match the instruction terms exactly. Decline and unknown reports may omit those two fields; supplied values are not used to establish completion.

The recorded statuses distinguish `requested` awaiting a guarantor outcome, `unknown` awaiting reconciliation, `completed` confirming the transfer, and `declined` recording a final refusal. Reconciliation uses the same request identifier. New outcomes are accepted only from `requested` or `unknown`; repeating a status requires the same reference and returns `duplicate`. Conflicting terminal outcomes are rejected.

Completion sets `/payment/completed` to the full instruction amount, copies the bank reference to `/payment/transactionId`, and emits Payment Completed with `evidence: bankConfirmation`, followed by a Transfer Outcome event. Decline and unknown reports update status and reference without recording completed money. The reference alone is not confirmation. `/payment/closed` is a separate request-control flag and is not set by this completion function. Refunds use separate transfer instructions.

Public transfer operations also invoke Require Active Parties; its underlying `requireActive` checks are not supplied.

## Inherited connection planning

Connections come from the containing clause's `type/actions`, or `parameters/actions` when `type/configurableActions` is `true`. Explicit `bindings` override `type/defaultBindings`; property bindings are checked against `type/bindingTypes`, with omissions permitted by `type/optionalBindings`. This plan declares no concrete data bindings of its own.

Action connections support `workflow`, `event`, `channel`, `embedded`, `collection`, `change`, `initialized`, `activated` and `timer` sources. Action `defaults` merge with connection `params`; connection `when` can skip execution, while action requirements and `parameters.conditions` can reject it. `before` and `after` surround the action. Declared preflight and `resultContract: outcome-v1` distinguish `acceptedNew`, `duplicate`, `rejected` and `skipped`, preventing later stages from treating every invocation as a new success. `once` defaults to `false`; when enabled, its fired marker is written after the permitted action stages finish.

Timer connections use either an absolute `timestamp` in Unix microseconds or a timestamped `afterEvent` with positive integral `delayMs`. Relative timers use `policy: first` by default or `latest`; initialization cannot supply their time base. Optional `cancelOn` emits a keyed cancellation. Emitting a timer request is separate from its processor-admitted firing.

The inherited `validateTransition` always refuses with `PAYMENT_PROCESS_POLICY_IMMUTABLE`. In the supplied clause host, this veto applies whenever the installed clause's transition hook is consulted, including amendments affecting other clauses.
